title: The Treasure Island Map
teaser: The map was drawn by someone with a nose, and X is closer than you think.
clue: The map was drawn by the most reliable explorer in the house, and it is not you.
reveal: Your fenced yard becomes an island. Your dog leads a slow survey and chooses the landmarks, you draw the map, and a second lap ends at the treasure.
objective: Draw a treasure map from the spots your dog chooses to stop at in your yard, then follow it on a second lap to find a toy.
instructions: Pick a secure space: your fenced yard. Check the ground is clear and dry and the weather is mild.

Lap one, the survey: walk slowly and let your dog lead. Every time they stop to sniff something for a few seconds, that is a landmark. Jot a quick sketch and a funny name ('Sniff Rock', 'Old Stump'), until you have three or four.
Back at the start, lay a map on a clipboard or paper and join the landmarks with a dotted line. Mark the last one with an X.

Plant the treasure at the X while your dog watches from a comfortable distance or waits with someone else: a favorite toy under a towel or a few leaves, in plain sight. Never leave your dog alone on the island.
Lap two, the treasure run: show your dog the map, then walk from landmark to landmark in order. Let them lead at a walk or easy trot. At each stop, wait twenty seconds. No racing, and no pulling.
At the X, let your dog find and uncover the treasure, and play with it for a minute. Then sit on the island and read the map back to them.
Keep the map somewhere you will see it.
twist: Your dog draws the map without knowing it: every landmark is a place they chose to stop, and you are just the cartographer.
variations: For a seated owner: use a small yard patch with two landmarks and sit while the dog browses.
For a dog who doesn't like to wait: skip the hiding and put the treasure under a towel at the X in plain view.
For a puppy: ask your vet before any outdoor ground, including your own yard. Until then, play the indoor hallway version with two landmarks.
For a rainy day: draw an island of your hallway, with the sofa, rug and door as landmarks.
completion: Your dog has led a lap, the treasure has been found and the map is drawn.
photoIdea: Photograph your dog sitting beside the X on the ground with the map next to them.
memoryPrompt: Which landmark did your dog pick that surprised you?
substitutes: No clipboard? Use a hardback book.
safety: Check the space for glass, sharp items and anything toxic before you start.
Check the fence is secure and keep your dog on a line if there is any gap; follow local rules.
Skip hot or icy weather, and never leave your dog unattended in the yard.
